claim: Anthropic requires all Claude users to be at least 18, and the mobile app enforces this via App Store / Play Store account age data.
quote: We require all users to be at least 18 years old to create and use a Claude account... the app store on your device (App Store or Play Store) has identified you as under 18 based on your account information.

claim: Claude email signup requires phone verification, but 'Continue with Google' bypasses it because Google provides a verified auth signal.
quote: Claude requires phone number verification, and you cannot skip this step during sign-up... When you sign in through Google, Anthropic receives a verified authentication signal, which removes the need for phone verification.

claim: Claude rejects VoIP, Google Voice and app-created numbers during phone verification, and access depends on supported locations.
quote: Anthropic explicitly says this branch does not accept VoIP numbers, Google Voice numbers, app-created numbers, or landlines... Consumer Claude access still depends on supported locations.

claim: ChatGPT requires users be 13+, with parental consent for 13-17, and for under-13 classroom use the interaction must be conducted by an adult.
quote: ChatGPT is not meant for children under 13... children ages 13 to 18 obtain parental consent before using ChatGPT... if you are using ChatGPT in the education context for children under 13, the actual interaction with ChatGPT must be conducted by an adult.

claim: OpenAI checks both IP geography and phone-number country at signup, blocking ~20 countries either by government ban or OpenAI policy.
quote: OpenAI restricts access to ChatGPT by both IP address and by the country origin of phone numbers used for verification. The two checks work independently, which means you need to address both to get past them.

claim: Bolt.new free tier needs no credit card, gives 300k daily / 1M monthly tokens and is open worldwide.
quote: You can sign up and get started without a credit card. Anyone can sign up on Bolt.new worldwide, and start building an app with AI.

claim: v0 / Vercel signup offers Google, GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, and Apple as 'Continue with' providers — GitHub is not forced.
quote: Continue with Google ... Continue with GitHub ... Continue with GitLab ... Continue with Bitbucket ... Continue with Apple

claim: v0 free plan requires no credit card, only a Vercel account and a small monthly credit pool.
quote: V0's Free plan is the easiest way to get a feel for what the platform can do: no credit card, just a Vercel account and a few included credits to play with.

claim: Cursor accepts email/password, Google, or GitHub for signup; Hobby tier is free with no credit card.
quote: You can create an account using your email and password, Google, or GitHub... 2,000 code completions and 50 slow premium model requests per month with no credit card required.

claim: Cursor Student Pro is free for one year but requires a .edu email or SheerID-style ID upload (3–7 business-day manual review) — a friction point for non-edu workshop attendees.
quote: Eligible university students get one free year of Cursor Pro... your Cursor account email must match your valid ".edu" university email.

claim: Cloudflare Turnstile disproportionately blocks users behind shared NAT, VPNs, or low-reputation IPs — relevant to classroom / café wifi.
quote: Shared or blacklisted IPs from VPNs, proxies, or hotel Wi-Fi can be misclassified, and when multiple users share an IP previously linked to abuse, Cloudflare increases CAPTCHA prompts.

claim: Turnstile 'challenge loops' on shared wifi often trace to clock skew, blocked third-party cookies, or browser extensions stripping JS.
quote: Device clock synchronization issues can cause token rejection, with this single issue causing the majority of unexplained CAPTCHA failures.

claim: Established vibe-coding workshops instruct learners to create Cursor and GitHub accounts 24–48 hours ahead, citing 30+ minute downloads and trial-clock concerns.
quote: A Cursor Pro account is required... a free 14-day Pro trial is offered on first signup... complete all setup 24-48 hours before course start... large downloads (30+ minutes possible).

claim: Schools commonly block ChatGPT at the network layer and US districts increasingly add it to filter blocklists, on top of the age-13/parental-consent ToS hurdle.
quote: School networks are designed to filter content that administrators consider distracting or inappropriate, and as ChatGPT has become more popular, an increasing number of school districts have added it to their block lists.

claim: Institutions sidestep individual-signup friction by issuing pre-provisioned AI Sandbox accounts that wrap GPT/Claude/Gemini behind SSO, removing per-student phone or payment gates.
quote: The AI Sandbox provides a secure environment to explore Generative AI, minimizing security and privacy risks... All degree students are automatically granted access.
